name: vale-vscode
description: The Vale linter extension for Visual Studio Code and editors based on Visual Studio Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: When running untrusted, linting still works, but settings that control which executable runs or trigger automatic synchronisation (the Vale binary path, config, sync-on-startup, and Docker image and arguments) are locked to your user-level configuration, and commands that explicitly run a process (Sync, Show Configuration, Show Readability Metrics, vocabulary add) are disabled until the workspace is trusted.

vale.valeCLI.path.markdownDescription: Absolute or relative path to the Vale binary, instead of the one managed by the language server. Supports `~`, `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`, and `${env:VAR}`. Bare executable names use `PATH`. Workspace-relative executable paths are ignored in Restricted Mode. Leave empty to use `#vale.valeCLI.installVale#` or the copy on your `$PATH`. Ignored when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.valeCLI.installVale.markdownDescription: Always use the copy of Vale that the language server downloads and manages, even if Vale is installed elsewhere. By default the extension uses the Vale on your `$PATH`, and only falls back to the managed copy when there isn't one. Ignored when `#vale.valeCLI.path#` is set or `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true. **Vale: Install or Update Vale** only affects the managed copy.

vale.valeCLI.config.markdownDescription: Absolute or relative path to a Vale config file. Supports `~`, `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`, and `${env:VAR}`. If empty, uses Vale's default search (`.vale.ini`, `_vale.ini`, or `.config/vale.ini`, searching upwards from the file). Use **Vale: Select Configuration File** to pick one.

vale.valeCLI.noGlobal.markdownDescription: Pass `--no-global` to every Vale call so that Vale ignores the user-level `.vale.ini` instead of merging it into the project configuration.

vale.valeCLI.syncOnStartup.markdownDescription: Run `vale sync` when the extension and language server starts, to download the packages your configuration lists.

vale.valeCLI.syncViaLanguageServer.markdownDescription: Run **Vale: Sync** through the language server instead of running `vale sync` directly, so it uses exactly the Vale and configuration the server lints with. You can't cancel the sync and its progress isn't shown, instead, the server reports the result in a message. This already happens when there is no Vale on your `$PATH`, and only the managed copy exists.

vale.docker.enabled.markdownDescription: Run Vale inside a Docker container instead of a local install. Overrides `#vale.valeCLI.installVale#` and `#vale.valeCLI.path#`. Requires a workspace folder on the local filesystem and Docker installed.

vale.docker.image.markdownDescription: Docker image to run Vale from. Only used when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.docker.extraArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments spliced into `docker run` before the image name, e.g. an additional `-v` mount for a styles directory that lives outside the workspace. Only used when `#vale.docker.enabled#` is true.

vale.valeCLI.lintOnChange.markdownDescription: Lint as you type. If disabled, Vale lints when a file is opened and when it is saved. Changing this restarts the language server.

vale.valeCLI.debounceMs.markdownDescription: How long typing has to settle before linting, in milliseconds. Only applies when `#vale.valeCLI.lintOnChange#` is enabled.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Inherits the `minAlertLevel` from the active configuration file.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `suggestion`, overriding any configuration files.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `warning`, overriding any configuration files.
Sets `minAlertLevel` to `error`, overriding any configuration files.
vale.valeCLI.minAlertLevel.markdownDescription: Defines from which level of errors and above to display in the problems output.

vale.enableSpellcheck.markdownDescription: Enable spell checking with Vale, using the built-in `Vale.Spelling` rule.

vale.valeCLI.filter.markdownDescription: A raw Vale filter expression (for example `.Line > 10`), combined with the minimum alert level and spell-checking filters using `and`. Requires Vale 3.10.0 or later.

vale.maxNumberOfProblems.markdownDescription: The maximum number of problems shown for one file. Set to `0` for no limit.

vale.doNotShowWarningForFileToBeSavedBef.markdownDescription: Do not show the warning that a file must be saved before **Vale: Show Readability Metrics** can read it.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Displays readability problems in the status bar.
Displays readability problems inline with other problems.
Displays readability problems both in the status bar and inline in the file.
vale.readabilityProblemLocation.markdownDescription: Determines where file-level readability problems are displayed.

vale.valeCLI.showMetrics.markdownDescription: Show a code lens at the top of each document with its metrics (word count, reading time, and so on). Changing this restarts the language server.

vale.vocabPath.markdownDescription: Name of the vocabulary folder used by **Vale: Add to Accept List** and **Vale: Add to Reject List**, relative to the `StylesPath`. For example, `MyVocab` uses `<StylesPath>/config/vocabularies/MyVocab/`.

vale.startOnLanguages.markdownDescription: Language IDs that start the Vale language server when a file in that language is open. The server also starts when the workspace has a Vale config file (`.vale.ini`, `_vale.ini`, or `.config/vale.ini`), when `#vale.valeCLI.config#` is set (including outside the workspace), or when you run a Vale command. Selecting a configuration while idle also starts the server. Add IDs such as `go` or `python` to lint comments in code files, or use `["*"]` to always start. Changing it starts the server if a matching file is already open.

enumDescriptions: Trace requests and responses, without their content.
Trace requests and responses including their content.
vale.trace.server.markdownDescription: Traces the communication between VS Code and the language server. Output appears in the **Vale Language Server** output channel.

scripts.validate: npm run compile && npm run lint && npm test && npm run webpack
